title: Cross-repository architecture review and evidence
intro: Your answers establish a project as one product workspace that may have multiple repos, and choose a deep but safe analysis that updates the bitácora only. This round settles how the review crosses repo boundaries and what evidence makes a finding trustworthy.
coverage: Goal and initial scope clear; cross-repository analysis, audit rigor, and incomplete-scan handling open

questions.text: For a project with frontend and backend repos, should the audit trace user flows and verify contracts across the boundary (API/DTOs, auth, data ownership, configuration and deployment), not just map each repo independently?

options.label: Yes; produce one product-level architecture and call out mismatches across repos
Map each repo separately and only document obvious links

questions.why: The project is the product spanning repositories, so the main architectural failures may sit between them.

questions.text: How should findings distinguish proven architectural failures from ideas?

options.label: Separate confirmed violations from risks and improvement opportunities; cite repo/path/line or config/test evidence, impact, confidence and a recommendation
Use one unranked list of observations
Report only findings that have an automated test proving them

questions.why: Architecture judgment needs evidence and uncertainty labels; not every important boundary problem is mechanically testable.

questions.text: Which heavy review process should it use?

options.label: Inventory every repo, analyze each repo, synthesize end-to-end flows/contracts, then run an independent architecture review and reconcile its findings
One agent reads the entire workspace once and writes the docs
Run a fixed number of review rounds even if findings are already stable

questions.why: It gives independent coverage and cross-repo synthesis without an arbitrary endless loop; existing explorer/reviewer roles can support it.

questions.text: What should happen when a repo is missing/inaccessible or a safe check cannot run?

options.label: Continue with the accessible repos, show a coverage matrix and limitations, and avoid claiming the audit is complete
Stop the whole process until every repo and check is available
Infer the missing repo from the other code and mark the audit complete

questions.why: Partial evidence can still help, as long as gaps are visible and no conclusion overstates coverage.

questions.text: Should the implementation add a dedicated CLI command such as `bitacora.py audit` for reruns, or keep this as an AI-guided workflow around the existing `init` plus a documented manual trigger?

options.label: Add a dedicated audit/onboarding entrypoint; the CLI orchestrates the process and the AI performs architectural judgment
Keep the current CLI and define the workflow only in SKILL.md/references
Make `init` itself perform all scanning and require AI context through hooks

questions.why: A clear entrypoint makes onboarding repeatable while keeping reasoning and findings in the agent instead of embedding LLM behavior in the Python CLI.

q1.note: Treat frontend and backend as one product and report cross-repository mismatches.

q2.note: Separate confirmed failures from risks and improvements, with evidence and confidence.

q3.note: Inventory, analyze each repo, synthesize the product, and run one independent architecture review.

q4.note: Continue with a coverage matrix and limitations; never claim completeness with gaps.

q5.note: Integrate onboarding for new bitácoras and an explicit rerun trigger; the AI performs the analysis while scripts provide deterministic inventory/context.
